articles.title: Music Assistant guides a household through its first setup
articles.dek: A guided setup connects sources and players, adapting to households that start music from their phone apps.
body: Music Assistant gives new administrators a guided route from an empty installation to a listening setup. The wizard asks how the household listens, then walks through music sources, players, optional plugins and a summary instead of leaving the administrator at a settings page.

People who prefer to start music from the apps on their phones can postpone adding music sources without blocking completion. A Getting started entry tracks unfinished steps, while the wizard skips completed work and can be opened again from settings.
Marcel van der Veldt builds the flow for administrators. A separate welcome flow for household members remains future work.

pullRequests.title: Guide new admins through setup with an onboarding wizard

articles.title: An NFC tag opens the Home Assistant control you need
articles.dek: The iPhone app writes a control-screen link to a contactless tag from its Add to menu.
body: Home Assistant’s iOS app adds a direct way to put a device or sensor’s control screen on an NFC tag. Choosing NFC Tag from its Add to menu writes the link to a nearby contactless tag; scanning it opens that item’s more-info dialog.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves connects the menu to the system’s tag-writing sheet, which guides the write and reports errors. The option appears only on devices with NFC available. The tag opens the control screen rather than running an action itself.

pullRequests.title: Add NFC Tag option to the entity "Add to" menu

articles.title: Music Assistant lets household members manage their own music
articles.dek: Members gain permission to connect their own sources, while playlist owners get a dialog for sharing and collaboration.
body: Music Assistant enables household members to add and manage their own music sources, closing a gap left by the account-sharing controls reported yesterday. Setting up local disk sources stays an administrator’s responsibility because it can read folders on the server.

Playlist owners also gain a Share dialog that chooses who can see a personal Music Assistant playlist and whether those people may add or remove tracks. Members can choose individual people when sharing their music sources, and the app follows their role’s permissions when showing actions.

A related safeguard keeps one person’s listening out of another person’s streaming history. When a listener owns an enabled account for a service, a busy or unavailable account produces an error instead of falling back to a partner’s account. Separate libraries such as local files, Plex and Jellyfin remain shareable.
articles.continuity: Yesterday’s sharing controls served administrators; this step gives members the permissions to manage their own sources and supplies the playlist-sharing interface.

articles.title: Home Assistant restricts two Synology power commands to administrators
articles.dek: Direct reboot and shutdown actions gain a permission check, while independently triggered automations keep working.
body: Home Assistant requires an administrator for the Synology DSM integration’s reboot and shutdown actions. A non-admin calling either action from a dashboard, developer tools or a manually started script or automation receives an Unauthorized error.

Franck Nijhof adds the check to those two actions. Automations and scripts running on their own triggers remain unaffected because their calls carry no user identity. The integration’s separate button entities are unchanged; the restriction applies to the two named actions.

articles.title: Home Connect hobs tell Home Assistant when the timer finishes
articles.dek: A correction restores missing event sensors, with a timer alarm verified on a Bosch hob.
body: A Home Connect hob’s timer can finish without its alarm ever reaching Home Assistant. The integration corrects an appliance-type mismatch that prevented four event sensors from being created for hobs, and Vincent Canuel verified the alarm-clock sensor end to end on a Bosch PVW81CHB1E.

The correction also creates the preheat and favorite-button sensors, but it does not guarantee that an appliance sends their events. The tested hob still supplied no favorite-button events through the public interface. Canuel makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the fix.
